newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 27.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The government's official announcement of its economic measures yesterday, coming after a marathon Cabinet meeting, dealt a blow to the weaker strata. The orginal plan for a wholesale abolition of tax exemptions has now been changed to a more gradual form but there are drastic cutbacks in benefits for large families. The government aims to cull a further 280 billion drachmas in revenues next year.
--The finance ministry has gone on the offensive, dramatically reducing interest rates on Treasury bills - to be issued on December 2 - to 11.5 percent.

--Fuel prices show a gradual de-escalation following Iraq's return to the international marekt. The events are a relief to the government which has been forced to intervene to contain the effects of rising fuel prices on inflation three times in the last half-year.

--The problems in the clearance of transactions at the stock exchange are due to the bad operation of the clearing house. Sources say the clearing house does not keep to deadlines and there are often delays of between 4-5 days.
IMERISIA

--Businesses are targeted to carry new burdens in the 1997 budget, the government says. The new tax measures announced by National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou yesterday include 10 measures that affect businesses and banks.

--The budget has provoked a storm of protest, with banks, public services and private firms shutting down tomorrow for 24 hours. Farmers will block national roads tomorrow. Unionists warn of more to come.
KERDOS
--Red tape preventing the clearance of transactions on the stock exchange within the strict deadline of 48 hours. The problem lies with the clearing house, which takes 72 hours to clear transactions.
--A capital gains tax on the sale of non-listed companies as well as 7.5 percent tax on interest on state titles are two of the new measures to be imposed.
--The government's bill also foresees a rise in the corporate tax rate to 40 percent from 35 percent and prepayment of tax by banks to 60 percent from the current 50 percent.
EXPRESS
--The government's seven new taxation measures will bring in 150 billion drachmas. Cabinet approved the measures despite a range of differing opinions during the four-hour meeting.
--Changes to development incentives are far-reaching.
--The objective tax criteria system will be extended to other firms and self-employed professionals.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The general strike called by the General Confederation of Workers of Greece (GSEE) and civil servants begins tomorrow as is expected to involve the private, as well as the public, sector.

--Five brokerage firms found themselves barred from the exchange yesterday for delaying clearance of transactions but the delays often appear to be the fault of the clearing house, rather than the firms.
--The Greek government is to devise as list of criteria to evaluate very low bids for public works projects, according to reports from Brussels. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
